text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MX-014","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"1) ALL JOINTS TO BE CO2 MIG, FULL WELDED.FILLET SIZE 10 mm."}],"comment":"Note N1 on page 1 requires full welding of all joints, but no dimensions are provided for machining the part after welding. Without post-weld machining dimensions the fabricator cannot guarantee the finished shaft meets its final size requirements. The designer should add a note or dimensions specifying which features are to be machined after welding.","recommended_correction":"Add a note such as 'MACHINE AFTER WELDING' with the relevant final dimensions, or explicitly dimension the post-weld machined surfaces."},{"rule_id":"WF-008","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"1) ALL JOINTS TO BE CO2 MIG, FULL WELDED.FILLET SIZE 10 mm."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"3) SUITABLE EDGE PREPARATION TO BE DONE."}],"comment":"Note N1 calls for full welds, but note N3 only vaguely states 'SUITABLE EDGE PREPARATION TO BE DONE' without dimensioning the bevel angle or root gap. For full-penetration welds the exact preparation geometry must be defined so the welder can achieve complete fusion; leaving it unspecified risks incomplete penetration and joint failure. The designer should replace the vague note with specific bevel angle and root gap dimensions or reference a detailed weld-prep standard.","recommended_correction":"Dimension the weld preparation (bevel angle, root face, root gap) directly on the drawing or cite a specific standard detail that defines them."}]}
